content.user_title: Draft GDPR Registers and DPIAs for Belgian SMEs
content.value_statement: Belgian SMEs need clear processing records and documented privacy risk assessments. This public guide helps structure Article 30 registers and Article 35 DPIA drafts.
actual_capabilities: Guides Article 30 register drafting for controller and processor roles.
Identifies five SME activity categories: payroll, customer management and invoicing, direct marketing, camera surveillance, and website analytics.
Outlines a three-gate DPIA obligation check using the Belgian GBA list, Article 35.3, and nine EDPB criteria.
Describes likelihood-times-impact risk scoring before and after mitigation measures.
Provides a short processing register example covering payroll, billing, and office cameras.
limitations: This folder contains only a public guide; original scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
Generated documents require DPO or privacy lawyer review and do not constitute legal advice.
The guide focuses on Belgian practice; other EU member states have separate national DPIA lists.
Data subject requests under Articles 15 to 21 are outside this skill.

use_cases.title: Prepare an SME processing register
use_cases.description: Draft activity entries for payroll, customer billing, and cameras, then identify missing facts for legal review.

use_cases.title: Document a DPIA obligation assessment
use_cases.description: Assess a proposed tool against the three named screening gates and document evidence gaps before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a DPIA working draft
use_cases.description: Structure privacy risks and mitigation measures for profiling or sensitive data processing, including residual risk for specialist review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a processing register
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an Article 30 controller register outline for my Belgian SME covering payroll and billing. Ask for missing facts and label assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a first register outline.

prompt_templates.title: Draft processor records
prompt_templates.prompt: Help draft Article 30.2 processor records for [service]. Ask about controllers, processing categories, transfers, and safeguards. Flag missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare records for a processor role.

prompt_templates.title: Screen a proposed project
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [project] against the Belgian GBA list, Article 35.3, and nine EDPB criteria. Request evidence and flag conclusions needing current source verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: document whether a project needs a DPIA.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a risk-scored DPIA
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a DPIA for [processing]. Define a likelihood-times-impact scale, compare initial and residual risks, propose measures, and flag Article 36 consultation questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a DPIA for DPO review.

output_examples.input: Outline a register entry for payroll at a Belgian SME.
output: Purpose: calculate wages and support employment obligations.
Information needed: employee data categories, recipients, service providers, transfers, and security measures.
Review needed: confirm the applicable legal basis and retention period before approval.

output_examples.input: Prepare a DPIA screening outline for a new customer profiling tool.
output: Describe the profiling purpose, affected people, data categories, and intended decisions.
Check the Belgian GBA mandatory list, Article 35.3, and the nine EDPB criteria.
Record supporting facts and unresolved questions for each gate.
Screening conclusion remains pending until the project facts and current regulatory criteria are verified.

best_practices: Describe actual processing activities and use anonymized examples instead of identifiable employee or customer records.
Verify current Belgian requirements, legal bases, and retention periods before approving generated documents.
Record assumptions and residual risks, then obtain DPO or privacy lawyer review.
anti_patterns: Treating example retention periods as universal legal requirements.
Assuming the public guide includes the original templates, scripts, or automated legal checks.
Declaring compliance or ruling out a DPIA without documented project facts and specialist review.

faq.question: Does this guide cover controller and processor registers?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Article 30 controller records and Article 30.2 processor records, but the original templates are not included.

faq.question: Which checks does the DPIA screening use?
faq.answer: The guide names the Belgian GBA mandatory list, Article 35.3, and nine EDPB criteria. Verify their current requirements separately.

faq.question: How does risk scoring work?
faq.answer: The guide describes likelihood multiplied by impact, evaluated before and after technical and organizational measures. It does not define a numerical scale.

faq.question: Are scripts or ready-made templates included?
faq.answer: No. This folder contains only SKILL.md. The guide explicitly excludes scripts, extension source, and templates from the original package.

faq.question: Can this replace legal advice or support every EU jurisdiction?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Belgian practice and produces working documents for specialist review. Other member states have separate national DPIA lists.

faq.question: Does this handle data subject access requests?
faq.answer: No. Requests under Articles 15 to 21 are excluded and assigned to the separate nex-gdpr skill.
